author: source_goal_cli_scout_r56
body:
# Source goal CLI scout findings

Root HEAD observed: `d64f475e23a7339c91aa280ff6e6679c27607875`. The working tree is broadly dirty before this scout, including `src/ladon/proof_search_cli.py`, `src/ladon/proof_search_terminal.py`, and new untracked `src/ladon/source_goal_capture.py`; do not interpret those current bytes as baseline. This scout did not edit product files.

## Existing API and path policy

`src/ladon/source_goal_capture.py` already exposes `SourceGoalCaptureRequest` / `capture_source_goal`. It requires an explicit pinned `LeanToolchainContext` for the identical resolved repo, rejects ambient selection and checks an optional `sha256:<lowerhex>` source fingerprint before running. Each helper invocation is bounded (defaults: 60s, 8MiB output, 32GiB RSS), runs via `run_bounded_target_process`, and capture performs two observations around import-closure/inventory hashing. It returns a v1 result with `captured` or a structured unavailable/stale/ambiguous result; operation is observation only. `_source_path` in `source_association_io.py` is the authoritative safe relative `.lean`/module path check; reuse it via API rather than implementing a weaker CLI path resolver. Existing API columns are zero-based Unicode scalar counts (Lean FileMap convention); line is one-based. The CLI contract should explicitly translate diagnostic positions before calling it.

## Lean position and goal-at support (authoritative pinned source)

Checked both installed sources `~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.1/src/lean/Lean/Data/Position.lean` and v4.33.0 equivalent. `Lean.Position` stores line and column. `FileMap.toPosition` counts with `String.Pos.next`, i.e. Unicode scalar values, while `FileMap.ofPosition` consumes a zero-based line/column. `Lean.mkErrorStringWithPos` in `Lean/Message.lean` directly renders `{fileName}:{pos.line}:{pos.column}` with no `+1`. Therefore Lean plain diagnostic line/column are 1-based line and 0-based scalar column at the message formatter level; the proposed contract's blanket “compiler text positions are 1-based scalar lines/columns” is incorrect for the column. Do not subtract 1 from its rendered column; feed as zero-based API column. A real process fixture could verify the end-to-end display, but no pinned compiler was run in this scout.

`Lean.Server.InfoUtils.InfoTree.goalsAt?` is the supported frontend source-goal lookup, not a generic position-to-term query. It returns `TacticInfo` ranges (with trailing trivia and an EOF exception), selects an innermost/priority result, and exposes before/after state with nested-tactic heuristics. The existing helper instead enumerates all produced trees and insists `found.size == 1`, deliberately reporting no-goal or ambiguous observations. The frontend path is ordinary non-modular `Language.Lean.process`; it disables async, supplies default Options, and rejects modular source. It records local options/open decls at the selected context but does not reconstruct Lake setup/plugin/editor state. Keep these scope limits explicit; a diagnostic's location may fail to overlap a TacticInfo range or may identify an expression context with no tactic state.

## Diagnostic parsing / source-bound honesty

`Lean.MessageData` is a tree of constructors (`ofFormatWithInfos`, `ofGoal`, `withContext`, `tagged`, `ofOriginatingSyntax`, lazy, etc.) whose ordinary terminal rendering loses constructor structure. `TermElabM` constructs user-facing mismatch prose (“has type … but is expected to have type …”) via pretty printing. Text is not a stable structured AST; classify narrowly around a documented rendered form and fail closed on unknown/multiline/ambiguous boundaries. Do not use error header alone. A constructor-field mismatch may represent application/declaration context and may not carry a tactic goal at that location. Parse expression, actual type, expected type as caller-provided fragments, retain exact stream/file digest and selected record coordinates, then attempt source capture independently. Keep parsed values even when capture is unavailable; never label expectedType as an observed goal. Require explicit ordinal when multiple qualifying records exist. A compiler path may only be normalized after resolving and proving it is within repo; reject outside-root, malformed, or source/module mismatch rather than inferring module from prettyprinted text.

## Suggested coverage / docs

Clarify position conversion: Lean rendered column zero-based; requested line one-based. Exercise ASCII plus multibyte Unicode scalar before the location; nested namespace/section/open and source-local `set_option`; repeated local names, dependent locals and let values; multiple goals/diagnostics and explicit ordinals; stale digest, no TacticInfo/no goal, unsupported modular source, out-of-repo diagnostic filenames, malformed or unsupported mismatch layout. Assert parsed diagnostic fragments survive a failed source-capture attempt and remain separate from actual capture. Document default setup/profile as ordinary frontend, capture scope and replay not run; text view foreground goal plus visible locals should reference canonical full JSON and flag internal locals separately.

## Commands / limits

Read-only commands: `sed`/`rg` on the files named above and Python SQLite select for post 624. No Lean process was run; no source-helper calls; no tests or builds; no shared build outputs touched. Working-tree dirtiness was observed with `git status --short` and belongs to the pre-existing broader task state.

body:
# Application-context scout (post #651)

Read-only source map against HEAD `d64f475e23a7339c91aa280ff6e6679c27607875`; no Lean/helper execution, source edits, tests, builds, or OpenSpec changes.

## Current capture gap and likely owner path

`src/ladon/lean/ladon_semantic_candidate_helper.lean` defines closed ToJson structures for `SemanticExpression` (`typeDisplay`, `typeStructural`), `SemanticLocalDecl`, `SemanticCandidateOutput`, and `SemanticBatchRow`. `analyzeApplication` (around lines 323–365) first calls `introduceForall`, captures `localContextTypes` from `focused`, applies the candidate, discharges exact local matches, then emits residuals by reading `residual.getType` and pretty/repr only. Thus the captured top-level context is the focused goal context before candidate application; no residual row owns an observed context. `dischargeResiduals` already enters each `residual.withContext`, so the precise extension point is there (sample ordered declarations while each residual is in its own context; preserve residual array order and do not infer a context from expression display). `localContextTypes` carries raw ordinal local refs, binder info, structural types/values, dependency refs, and declaration origin; use its output as identity-bearing local data rather than names alone.

The selected declaration type is already available as `candidateInfo.type`, while public `candidate` subject is generated with `subject ... candidateLeanName`. A declaration binder inventory should be derived by Lean Meta traversal of that elaborated type, preserving telescope order, each binder's explicit/implicit/instance `BinderInfo`, and the instantiated domain type under earlier locals. It is a view of the declaration's type, not a claim that rows are necessary assumptions. Current helper's `applicationSubstitutions` manually walks forall args and only emits consumed application arguments; that is not a complete telescope/binder inventory.

## Strict protocol and consumers

Python single candidate constants are in `semantic_candidate_worker.py` (`SEMANTIC_PROTOCOL`, `SEMANTIC_BATCH_PROTOCOL`); closed application validation is in `semantic_candidate_protocol.py:validate_application_rows`. Single worker checks exact protocol and required fields in `_validate_worker_frame`, then validates collections, caller-observed top-level context, application rows, and identities in `_parse_worker_payload`. Rejection frames have a separate exact field set and must remain valid under a new version. Batch framing/identity and row fields are separately strict in `semantic_candidate_batch_worker.py` (`_validate_batch_frame`, `_validate_batch_semantic_population`, `_validate_batch_row_shape`, `_validate_batch_row_evidence`); header currently has only the top-level local context, and each candidate row currently has residual expressions without residual contexts or declaration inventory. Both transports must evolve coherently.

Important independent binding point: `semantic_candidate_worker._application_subject` derives candidate-application identity from statement/declaration refs, residual statement refs, substitutions, one top-level local-context ref, discharge rows and application text. Its `searchShape` repeats residual rows and top-level context but has no per-residual owner. `_context_subject` fingerprints ordered locals with environment ref and raw local IDs/dependencies. A v4 extension must bind each residual context into the application content identity (and retain order), not merely add display fields. `_semantic_observation_results.py` validates candidate shape consistency; `_semantic_observation_contract.py` validates receipt/context ownership; `semantic_stored_receipt.py` reconstructs/reads the compact application fields. Those are likely update points for v4 semantics and historical behavior.

`semantic_projection_cards.py` projects only `applicationTerm`, substitutions, residualPremises and discharged rows today. `_semantic_rows` sanitizes row mappings under projection bounds. Additive per-residual contexts and binder inventory need deliberate projection policy and omissions, with exact registry expansion links retained; do not put unbounded Lean text into compact cards.

ProofIR ownership is generic: `proofir_v3.py` validates subject `searchShape` as an object but semantic ownership/shape constraints live in the semantic observation modules above. `semantic_evidence_registry.py` stores/resolves validated artifacts; it should preserve old canonical v3 bytes. Historical v3 payloads lacking the new per-residual observations cannot be upgraded by projection/reconstruction and must remain readable as v3 while any request for v4 completion/extraction reports unavailable. Never fabricate missing contexts or mark them v4. No need appears to rewrite every old artifact or claim old contexts.

## Candidate contract and fixture

Minimal strict protocol contract tests can exercise a fully populated v4 single terminal frame and v4 batch header/row, reject missing residual contexts, reject reordered/malformed local identities and duplicate/unknown context local refs, and verify old v3 remains accepted only through its existing legacy stored-reader path—not the v4 extraction path. Unit tests can validate canonical digest binding: changing one residual context local structural type/value/dependency or its order changes candidate-application identity; changing only display text should follow the repo's existing structural identity convention.

For real Lean integration, extend `tests/test_semantic_candidate_residual_integration.py` / `tests/test_semantic_application_binding_integration.py` with a standalone Lean file and no Mathlib. Use dependent locals (`α : Type`, `x : α`, `h : R x`), a local `let` depending on an earlier same-named local, and candidate `And.intro` or a small polymorphic declaration yielding two ordered residuals. Assert the returned residual order, each residual's actual context rows and raw `local:*` identities, dependency/order preservation, plus a selected declaration with one explicit parameter, one implicit parameter and one instance binder. Prefer adding a focused fixture under existing supported installed-Lean integration route. Portable closed-frame tests should be the red gate; installed Lean test proves helper observation.

## Validation commands to consider (not run)

`uv run --locked pytest -q tests/test_semantic_candidate_framed_protocol.py tests/test_semantic_candidate_batch_worker.py tests/test_semantic_candidate_worker_v3_contract.py tests/test_semantic_candidate_residual_integration.py tests/test_semantic_application_binding_integration.py tests/test_semantic_binding_projection.py tests/test_semantic_observation_closure.py tests/test_semantic_result_projection.py tests/test_semantic_evidence_registry.py tests/test_semantic_candidate_lean_integration.py`

No commands above were executed. This is an API/dependency map and proposal, not implementation or acceptance evidence.
